$comment: Dematic's DA50 15.8 s copy of the Cencora world, for the runs that time the DA50 by the fixed cycle of Dematic's DA50 baseline rather than by the spec sheet: cencora_v3.json, the hand-managed document of record, with the DA50 class's fork and alignment times set to pick 7.1 s, drop 5.3 s and 1.7 s of alignment before each insertion, and nothing else changed. Make any other edit in cencora_v3.json and repeat it in cencora_v3_da50_baseline.json and cencora_v3_da50_sens6.json; scripts/add_cencora_aisles.py cuts the 21-aisle document from cencora_v3_da50_baseline.json. The rest of this comment is the record's own: Every hole belongs to the tiling it is a hole in: a region states the floor it has, and its own `exclusions` state the parts of that floor the building does not — nothing reaches across to subtract cells from a tiling it does not own. The relay lanes are not stated as floor at all but as open-cell patches, one per bay in each gap between rack sandwiches, with seams declared between patches. Each rack bay also declares three terminal HTM access cells under its relay boards, explicitly bound to both shelf levels and linked to the adjacent lane. VTM aisles do not declare HTM floor. Legacy identifiers ride as external_ids, never as identity.

frame.$comment: The old grid's rows, and so this floor's +y, run down the drawing. The site frame is drawn north-up, like the DWG-derived DFW6 document, so the floor mirrors into it: site y = 79140 - floor y, the floor's top edge landing at 0. The legacy grid below stays positive because it is stated in this floor, not in the site.

The old fixture's grid: 153 wide x 96 deep, cell_size_mm 850. An old index names a cell, and a cell's place is its centre, so index [c,r] reads as millimetres [850c+425, 850r+425]: the pitch as the scale, half a cell as the translation. Declared for projection only — nothing below is positioned in it. The scale is positive: desmap fixtures are self-consistent, unlike the Map Creator exports that need a mirror, and the half-cell offset is positive with it.

template.$comment: One bay, presenting its boards on the `+y` face. That face is on the steel because it is a fact about the steel; which face the STORAGE is worked from, and by whom, is the access declared beside each run. The old `sides` enum said both at once and named one.

rack.$comment: Old racks["cencora_a5_bay"], read back out of its slot list: 4 distinct x positions are slot columns, 11 distinct heights are shelf levels, 1 slot(s) at each position is the depth, and the diving-board slots are relay levels, grouped by diving_board_slot so a stack is two shelves at one position on the bay. All 13 heights stand in one list, bottom-up, exactly where the prototype surveyed them — there is no pitch to assert and nothing to disagree with. The across-run depth, and how far a relay reaches for the cell an HTM stands on, are the numbers the old prototype has nowhere to state and are converter parameters.

robot_class.$comment: The old file's entire robot model is a count. Dimensions are representative; see the fixture's ledger for every invented value. No `lineage`: nobody is named as having built this class, so nobody is named.

end_effector.$comment: The A5 tool gives the fork type as 'hooked boxes, 3-deep and within'; its depth table times a 2-deep pick at 23.59 s and a 3-deep one at 39.94 s, relocation included. Pick, drop and alignment here make the 15.8 s fixed cycle of Dematic's DA50 baseline (7.1 + 5.3 + 1.7 + 1.7 s), in place of the 17.2 s that cencora_v3.json takes from the DA50 spec sheet's rows 1, 2 and 8 (6.2, 5.0 and 3.0 s). The simulator scans before every fork insertion, as issue #262 decided; whether the scan belongs to the approach alone is still unconfirmed.

template.$comment: One bay's worth of HTM standing room in a gap between rack sandwiches: 3 rows at the boards' own 645 mm spacing, `width` columns of 850 across the gap. The floor exists only where the work is — the aisles between these patches carry no cells, so nothing has to carve them back out afterwards. Every gap in this building takes the same 4 columns; `width` is a parameter because the next building's need not.
